sheet-1.description: The map part of sheet 1, below the heavy rule that separates it from the index and key map, shows the southern part of Yardville Heights, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch. Grandview Avenue crosses the top of the part and Springdale Avenue the lower middle. Three streets run north to south between them: Althea Avenue, Frederick Avenue and Forest Avenue, with Highland Avenue near the right edge. Burnside Avenue joins Althea and Frederick Avenues from the west. Crosswicks Creek winds down the left edge, beside blocks 107 and 113, and the block numbers 108 to 110 and 114 mark the subdivision blocks. The ground is a paper subdivision: the blocks are ruled into narrow lots, most of them empty, with a few frame dwellings and sheds, mostly yellow, scattered along the streets and one or two buildings near the right edge. A street at the lower left, west of Frederick Avenue, is marked 'Not Named - Not Open'. Street widths of 25, 30 and 40 feet are marked. The bottom edge is lettered 'No Exposure'. A compass rose stands at the right edge and the scale bar at the lower left. The block continues on sheet 8, whose number is printed at the top of the map.
notes: Forest Avenue is today Soden Drive; Springdale Avenue is today Mount Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Only the map below the heavy rule is this part; the index, legend and 900-ft key map above it are not mapped.
A street west of Frederick Avenue is printed 'Not Named - Not Open'.

Printed sheet 1, top half: index, legend, NJ location map and key map at 900 ft to an inch (not a part). Below the heavy rule: one map part at 100 ft, Yardville Heights south of Grandview Avenue: Althea, Frederick, Forest (today Soden Drive), Highland Avenues, Burnside and Springdale (today Mount Avenue) Avenues, Crosswicks Creek on the west. Two scans: canvas-01 is the duplicate.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the south-eastern edge of the built-up part of White Horse, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch and drawn with north towards the upper left. The densest part is the upper left, where Clinton crosses the top and Maple Shade Avenue runs down the west edge; White Horse Avenue runs down from Clinton to the road junction at the centre left, with St. Raphael's Church (Roman Catholic) and a Fire Department building near the top. Locust Avenue and Lacy Avenue, with narrow building lots ruled across blocks 54 and 55, run up to the right from the neighbourhood of South Broad, which crosses the sheet as a wide diagonal street and meets Bordentown Road and White Horse Avenue at the former White Horse junction. Below that junction, Parent Avenue, Rulf Avenue and Zoar Avenue carry rows of small frame dwellings in blocks 72 to 75, with Pearsonville M. E. Church on the east side of Bordentown Road. Ruskin, Linden, Alfred and Camden Avenues and Acton Place appear at the lower left. The large right-hand and lower parts of the sheet are open farmland lettered with block numbers 76 and 77, except for the Bordentown Water Works with its tank and well near the right edge, and a few farm buildings. Bordentown Road leaves the junction to the south-east. Edges outside the drawn area are lettered 'No Exposure'.
notes: Clinton is today South Clinton Avenue; South Broad is today South Broad Street; White Horse Avenue is today Whitehorse Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
The White Horse junction of South Broad, Bordentown Road and White Horse Avenue is today a traffic circle (White Horse Circle); its junctions were not used as control.
Locust Avenue / Whitehorse Avenue was left out of the fit: the drawn White Horse Avenue is about 38 ft wide there against 55 ft today and the modern node lies 4 to 5 m from the drawn junction.
Parent Avenue / South Broad Street was left out (4.6 m residual beside the circle).
Names were read on the 1600-pixel overview and checked on full-resolution crops only for the Ruskin, Rulf, Zoar and Linden lettering.

Printed sheet 2, 100 ft. South Broad Street and Bordentown Road south-east of the White Horse junction (today White Horse Circle): St. Raphael's Church, Bordentown Water Works, Zoar, Rulf, Clinton, Lincoln, Locust; much open land. The old White Horse junction is today White Horse Circle (not used); Locust / Whitehorse and Parent / South Broad excluded (4.6 to 4.8 m).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the south-western part of White Horse, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch and drawn with north towards the upper left. Clinton crosses the top of the sheet. Beneath it the wide diagonal of South Broad separates the large, mostly empty blocks 49 to 52 above (Fernwood, Woodside, Homestead, Colonial and Maple Shade Avenues, with long narrow lots and houses along their southern fronts) from the densely lotted blocks 57 to 63 below, where Dewey Avenue, Hobson Avenue and the cross streets Miles, Oregon, Olympia, Bismark and Victoria Avenues carry rows of small frame dwellings. The De-Cou Public School stands at the left. A very large block, 65, holds Colonial Cemetery with a compass rose; to its south Ruskin, Linden and Alfred Avenues run across the lower right in blocks 66 to 68, ending at Camden Avenue, with Cliff Avenue and Parent Avenue at the right edge. Acton Place and an electric railway cross the bottom, with Powell Place and Shibla Avenue and blocks 69 and 70 beyond; a Fairview greenhouse building and a fire department building appear among the blocks. Lettering 'No Exposure' marks the unmapped edges.
notes: Fernwood Avenue is today Redwood Avenue; Clinton is today South Clinton Avenue; South Broad is today South Broad Street (OpenStreetMap).
A street at the lower left is lettered only 'Street' and 'Not Named'.
Fernwood Avenue is lettered 'Not Open' in places and its junctions carry residuals of 3 to 4 m.
Dewey Avenue / South Broad Street was left out of the fit (4.8 m residual).
Names were read on the 1600-pixel overview, not on full-resolution crops.

Printed sheet 3, 100 ft. Dense south-west grid: South Broad, Olympia, Oregon, Bismark, Ruskin, Linden, Victoria, Alfred, Acton Place, Dewey, Hobson, Woodside, Homestead, Maple Shade, Camden; Fairview Greenhouse, De-Cou Public School.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 lies north-east of sheet 5 and shows the northern part of White Horse, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch and drawn with north towards the upper left. White Horse Avenue runs the full height of the sheet, with Orchid Avenue, McGalliard Avenue and Exton Avenue crossing it from the west and Maple Shade Avenue along the left edge; Clinton closes the bottom left. East of White Horse Avenue the east part of McGalliard Avenue runs across to Gropp Avenue, which is lettered 'Not Opened' beside Lacy Avenue, and a row of houses with numbers from 1920 to 2060 stands along its north side. Most of the ground between is long, narrow plots of blocks 27 and 43 to 46, mostly empty, with a greenhouse, a dairy and milk bottling works, and a private road. Phillips and Locust Avenues run up diagonally across the lower right to Lacy Avenue, with Locust Avenue crossing near the sheet's lower edge. The compass rose is at upper right; the top and parts of the right edge are lettered 'No Exposure' and 'Not Open'.
notes: Orchid Avenue is today Orchard Avenue; Clinton is today South Clinton Avenue; White Horse Avenue is today Whitehorse Avenue; South Broad is today South Broad Street (OpenStreetMap).
McGalliard Avenue jogs at White Horse Avenue: the west part is drawn about 85 px lower than the east part, matching McGalliard Avenue and East McGalliard Avenue today.
Locust Avenue / Whitehorse Avenue was left out of the fit (4.6 m residual).
Gropp Avenue / Locust Avenue was rejected (about 9 to 10 m).
Names were read on the 1600-pixel overview, not on full-resolution crops.

Printed sheet 4, 100 ft. East of sheet 5: McGalliard, Phillips, Locust, Clinton, White Horse Avenue (today Whitehorse Avenue), Lacy, Gropp, Maple Shade, Garden. McGalliard jogs at White Horse Avenue (west part McGalliard Avenue, east part East McGalliard Avenue). Locust / Whitehorse excluded, Gropp / Locust rejected.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the north-western residential grid of White Horse, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with north towards the upper left. It runs from Spruce along the top edge down to Clinton along the bottom edge, and from Fernwood Avenue on the west edge across Woodside Avenue, Homestead Avenue and Colonial Avenue to Maple Shade Avenue on the east edge, with Orchid Avenue, McGalliard Avenue and Exton Avenue as the cross streets between. The ground is a recent suburban subdivision: long, narrow building lots ruled across blocks 28 to 41, most of them still empty. Development is concentrated in rows of small frame dwellings, many with frame garages or sheds behind, along the north side of Orchid Avenue, both sides of McGalliard Avenue near Colonial Avenue, and both sides of Exton Avenue, with a few brick and concrete-block buildings among them. House numbers in the 1700s and 1800s are printed along McGalliard and Exton. Points marked 'Private T.H.' stand at the corners of Colonial Avenue with McGalliard and Exton Avenues. The upper left of the sheet, blocks 28 and 29 north of Orchid Avenue, is blank apart from the compass rose and is lettered 'No Exposure'. Near Clinton at the bottom, a few storage sheds stand east of Homestead Avenue and a short stretch is marked 'Not Opened'. The street pattern is a regular rectangular grid, and almost all of the streets survive under the same names today.
notes: Fernwood Avenue is today Redwood Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Orchid Avenue is today Orchard Avenue.
Spruce is today Spruce Street; Clinton is today South Clinton Avenue.
Arena Drive, between Orchard and McGalliard Avenues today, is not on the sheet.
Fernwood Avenue runs along the west edge with only its east side drawn.

Printed sheet 5, 100 ft. North-west grid: Spruce, Orchid (Orchard Avenue), McGalliard, Exton, Clinton (South Clinton Avenue); Fernwood (today Redwood Avenue), Woodside, Homestead, Colonial, Maple Shade. Pilot sheet. Top left blank ('No Exposure').

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the northern outskirts of White Horse, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch and drawn with north towards the upper left. White Horse Avenue runs up the sheet from the bottom edge to a point near the top, where it meets the diagonal Hamilton Square Road, which crosses the right half from the lower centre to the upper right. West of White Horse Avenue lie the small suburban blocks 16 to 23, laid out in long narrow lots between Taft, Quimey, Bradford, Chapman, Knapp and Milton Avenues, with Garden Avenue running down the left side and bending south-east. Most lots are empty and the few houses are frame dwellings. Spruce crosses the lower part, with Colonial Avenue at the lower left, and blocks 26 and 30 beyond hold a row of dwellings. Maple Shade Public School stands on White Horse Avenue near Milton Avenue. East of White Horse Avenue the ground is large open tracts, blocks 24, 25 and 27, with Sharp Avenue laid out on the right with house numbers and a few farm buildings along Hamilton Square Road. A compass rose is at top centre; the left and right edges are lettered 'No Exposure'.
notes: Quimey Avenue is today Quimby Avenue; Spruce is today Spruce Street; White Horse Avenue is today Whitehorse Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Garden Avenue survives, but its modern line is displaced from the drawn one by 4 to 10 m at every junction, so it was left out of the fit.
Sharp Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Names were read on the 1600-pixel overview, plus one full-resolution check of Quimey.

Printed sheet 6, 100 ft. North: Taft, Quimey, Sharp, Knapp, Chapman, Milton, Spruce, Hamilton Square Road diagonal; Maple Shade Public School. Quimey is today Quimby Avenue. Garden Avenue left out: drawn with a jog, its junctions 3 to 9.5 m off (adding it raised LOO to 4.4 m). Seven of eight points lie along Whitehorse Avenue (LOO 119 m is a collinearity artefact); Colonial / Spruce agrees with sheet 5 to 0.8 m and the seam with sheet 5 to 0.4 m. Low-medium confidence.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northern part of Yardville Heights and the Hutchinson's Lake valley, in Hamilton Township, at 100 feet to an inch. South Broad crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right, passing over the narrow neck of Hutchinson's Lake on a wooden bridge on a steel frame; the lake and the winding creek that feeds it fill the upper centre, with Crosswicks Creek running down the left edge. In the upper left a corner of the Lakeside subdivision is drawn, with Lakeside Boulevard running down to South Broad between long narrow lots, a few frame dwellings and, near the bridge, a building lettered 'V.H.C.'. East of the lake the Yardville Heights Public School, in pink brick with its toilets and outbuildings, stands in a large block, block 101, north of South Broad. The lower half of the sheet is the Yardville Heights subdivision: Althea Avenue, Forest Avenue and Highland Avenue run north from Grandview Avenue to Prospect Avenue, and Highland Avenue continues north to South Broad. The blocks between, numbered 102 to 106, are ruled into narrow lots, most of them vacant; the dwellings, mostly yellow frame, stand in scattered rows, with a greenhouse and a few barns. The street widths are marked 30 feet and 40 feet. The upper right and the left and right edges are lettered 'No Exposure'. The compass rose is in the upper centre.
notes: Forest Avenue is today Soden Drive (OpenStreetMap).
South Broad is South Broad Street today; the road changes name to Bordentown Road / US 206 elsewhere.
Lakeside Boulevard survives today under the same name, but the Lakeside streets drawn on sheet 7 do not.
Yardville Heights Public School: the surviving building is not checked against the modern site.

Printed sheet 8, 100 ft. Yardville Heights north of Grandview Avenue: South Broad Street crossing Hutchinson's Lake, Lakeside Boulevard, Prospect, Althea, Forest (Soden Drive), Highland Avenues; Yardville Heights Public School; Crosswicks Creek. Drawn about -33 degrees (sheet 1 -28), square to the Yardville Heights grid, not the town's -21 to -23.
